title: Exclude single-route and fixed two-direction BIT repairs for packet 971
body:
Two exact screens cover the projected three-omission BIT candidate. All seven named single-route changes fail within the stated one-direction grammar. With routes and clocks fixed, all 678 possible surviving unit second directions fail.

## Scope and source

Identifies x341 with x340, drops 968, 971 and 1564, and retains protected output rows and 3553=x411. Includes 668 independently checked XOR witnesses and ten independently exhausted stock cores. Mixed directions and simultaneous altered routes lie outside these scopes. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit971-retarget-parity/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. Both inner archives passed their cold runs. The single-route README lists the literal word, first-read, parity, and 1,272-receiver checks. The second uses `python3 verify.py` to reproduce all 678 proofs. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Obtain a literal protected operator with a different paid roster or route/timing and reprice it. The prospective three-omission saving is unrealized.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
